name: veyq
//: Repo-root manifest for ONE reason: npm workspaces, so `src/web/` and `src/admin-web/` resolve the same `@veyq/crypto` on disk instead of each carrying a copy (ADR 0065 — duplicating the crypto suite would be a security defect, not a maintenance nuisance). It is deliberately not a build orchestrator: each surface keeps its own `npm run check` and is proven on its own, and nothing here aggregates them. Adding a workspace is the whole feature set.
//engines: The Node the workspace supports, stated so a wrong local one is named once, here, instead of as one EBADENGINE warning per package (inbox #353). It is the intersection of what the locked tree declares (measured 2026-10-10: abbrev and nopt `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`, the eslint family `^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24`, vitest `^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0`). The images and CI run Node 22 (the Dockerfiles' `node:22-bookworm-slim`, the workflows' `node-version: "22"`); an odd, non-LTS release such as 23 is outside every one of those ranges.
//lockfile: Bumping by hand (no remote, so no Dependabot): raise the floor in the workspace's package.json to the fixed version, then let npm re-resolve — never `--force`/`--legacy-peer-deps`. Two traps measured 2026-10-11 (inbox #403). (1) A package shared by src/web/ and src/admin-web/ must stay ONE hoisted copy: when both workspaces' ranges move past the root copy, npm nests a new copy per workspace (src/web/node_modules/vue …) and keeps the old one at the root, where every hoisted peer-dependent (primevue, vue-i18n, @vitejs/plugin-vue) still resolves — two Vue runtimes in one bundle. Check `git diff package-lock.json` for new `src/web/node_modules/` or `src/admin-web/node_modules/` entries; if one appears, drop that package's entries (root and nested) from the lockfile and install again so it is re-placed once at the root. Such nesting is also what made `npm audit fix` fail with ERESOLVE on `@vue/test-utils` (a copy nested per workspace against the root vue). (2) npm 10.9.x (Node 22's bundled npm, 10.9.9 included) crashes re-resolving vitest's peer set here (`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`); run that one install with `npx -y npm@11 install`, then a plain npm 10 `npm install` so the lockfile keeps the `dev` flags the CI npm writes. `npm ci` with npm 10 reads the result unchanged. (3) A NEW override on a package already in the lockfile is not applied by `npm install` (npm 10 or 11): the locked copy stays and `npm ls` calls it invalid; deleting its lockfile entry instead makes npm 10 prune the whole chain above it (measured 2026-10-30, basic-ftp under get-uri). `npm update <that package>` re-places it under the override in one step, with a clean diff.
//overrides: MOVED here from src/web/package.json when the workspace was introduced (cr-admin-web-extraction): npm honours `overrides` only from the workspace ROOT, so leaving it in src/web/ would have silently stopped applying — a knowingly-vulnerable transitive dep back in the tree with no signal. qs: @stryker-mutator/core@9 -> typed-rest-client@~2.3.0 (2.3.1) pins qs at EXACTLY 6.15.1. That exact pin — not a range — is why `npm audit fix` cannot resolve it without --force. The floor has moved with the advisories: 6.15.1 carried GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26 (qs.stringify DoS, fixed 6.15.2); then GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx (array-limit bypass, <=6.15.3) and GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g (isBuffer DoS, <6.16.0) made 6.16.0 the first clean one (inbox #403); then GHSA-6pq8-jhm2-2vcw (stringify arrayFormat 'comma' TypeError DoS, <=6.16.0) made it 6.16.1 (inbox #805, 2026-10-30). The vulnerable path is unreachable here (typed-rest-client only serves Stryker's dashboard reporter, which stryker.config.mjs does not enable), but a knowingly-vulnerable dependency is not something we keep. Drop this override once Stryker depends on a typed-rest-client that requires qs >= 6.16.1 (none does yet, measured 2026-10-30: Stryker 9.6.1 and 10.1.1 still pin typed-rest-client ~2.3.0, and even typed-rest-client 3.1.2 asks only qs ^6.16.0, which still admits the vulnerable 6.16.0). basic-ftp (added 2026-10-30, inbox #805): @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli@2.41.0 and 2.42.0 pin proxy-agent at EXACTLY 8.0.2 -> pac-proxy-agent 9.1.0 -> get-uri EXACTLY 8.0.1 (the latest) -> basic-ftp ^5.3.1, and every 5.x carries GHSA-c475-qrg2-pj4r (Client.list() directory-listing parser quadratic-time DoS, <=6.2.0, fixed 6.2.1) — so only an override reaches the fix. It is a major: basic-ftp 6.0.0 refuses a separate transfer host by default (FTP bounce protection); every Client call get-uri makes (access, lastMod, list, downloadTo, close) keeps its 5.x signature, and the path is unreachable here anyway (get-uri's ftp: scheme serves a PAC file fetched over ftp://, which no generator run configures). Drop this override once get-uri depends on basic-ftp >= 6.2.1 and the generator's proxy-agent pin reaches that get-uri.
